entity_scope: OAO LUKOIL Group; Getty Petroleum Marketing Inc.
observation: The Group reports acquiring 72 percent of Getty Petroleum Marketing Inc. in December 2000 for 53 million US dollars.
limits: First component of one acquisition group, not entire takeover price. Rounded issuer accounting disclosure, not bank instrument, individual seller receipt or Trump-linked flow.

entity_scope: OAO LUKOIL Group; Getty Petroleum Marketing Inc.
observation: The Group reports acquiring the remaining 28 percent in January 2001 for 20 million US dollars, increasing ownership to 100 percent.
limits: Second component of same acquisition. Not an additional transaction beyond the derived 73 million combined amount; not the unrelated Getty Realty debt balance or proved bank-cleared remittance.

entity_scope: OAO LUKOIL Group; Getty Petroleum Marketing Inc.
observation: Reported rounded components imply approximately 73 million US dollars for the full equity acquisition.
limits: Derived summary, never a third payment. Do not add this row to either component; no fee, debt, property-title or seller-allocation reconciliation.

entity_scope: Getty Realty; Getty Petroleum Marketing Inc.; subsidiary of OAO Lukoil
observation: Getty Realty reports that a Lukoil subsidiary acquired approximately 72 percent of Marketing common stock by December 8 tender and the remaining equity by January 25 merger.
limits: Independent issuer description of same acquisition, not a new payment. Subsidiary identity not independently resolved here; dates are not inferred from filing date.

entity_scope: Getty Realty; Getty Petroleum Marketing Inc.
observation: Getty Realty describes itself as owner/lessor of stations, convenience stores and terminals, leasing most properties to Marketing after its March 21, 1997 spin-off. Amended master lease effective December 9, 2000 has an initial fifteen-year term.
limits: Marketing equity acquisition did not itself convey Getty Realty property ownership. Leased operational access is not fee title; no blanket claim that every Marketing property was leased and no rent cash total derived.

pages_or_locator: Brent Coscia testimony to Judiciary Committee
observation: Coscia identifies himself as Consumers Petroleum director of sales and opposes raised S.B.1426 as a change to the divorcement framework.
limits: Professional self-identification and policy opposition are not a corporate-identifier match to every later Consumers entity or measured real-world outcomes.

entity_scope: Vincent DeLaurentis; Getty Petroleum Marketing, Inc.
pages_or_locator: DeLaurentis testimony and Cappiello / O Neill questions
observation: Getty president/COO describes 92 Connecticut stations supplied, including 74 commission arrangements; dealers run sites while Getty sets gasoline price. He describes domestic-refiner purchases, not purchases from its foreign parent.
limits: Source occasionally prints 74 or 92; contextual reading is 74 commission arrangements among 92 supplied stations. Testimony is not an independently inspected contract/site census. No Russian-origin fuel or all-company station ownership inference.

entity_scope: Getty Petroleum Marketing, Inc.; commission operators; Connecticut petroleum market
pages_or_locator: DeLaurentis opening statement; William Hawthorne testimony
observation: Getty and a supporting operator described supply availability, lower dealer inventory-capital burdens and continuity of small-business commission arrangements as reasons to support the proposal.
limits: Attributed commercial arguments, not verified volume, savings, profitability, station survival or effect of enacted relief.

entity_scope: Connecticut raised S.B.1426; qualifying producer/refiner acquirers and distributors
pages_or_locator: Introduced bill sections 1-3; official bill history
observation: Proposed section 14-344a(b) covers producer/refiner acquisitions on or after January 1, 2001 of distributors doing business in Connecticut on January 1, 2001 through independent-contractor commission sales, permitting them to continue to open and operate stations. Section 2 would repeal 14-344b; proposed effective date July 1, 2001.
limits: Proposal only, broader than preservation of the existing 74 arrangements. Not enacted permission, an effective-date finding, a Getty-only named exemption or proof of any resulting commercial benefit.

observation: Displayed history lists March 26 referral to Judiciary and March 29 Public Hearing 04/02. No favorable report, passage or act number appears in the acquired status record.
limits: Displayed record boundary, not a verified rejection vote or exact committee-burial date. April 2 actual hearing is independently documented by S003.

pages_or_locator: 2025 chapter 250a sections 14-344a/b and act histories; May 2, 2006 OLR report
observation: 2025 text retains section 14-344b and contains no proposed acquisition exception; both a and b cite only P.A.79-437. The 2006 OLR report also treats both restrictions as operative. Together with bill history this supports not enacted as introduced.
limits: Do not infer a particular defeat vote, enforcement action or Getty-specific regulatory disposition. This is a 2025 codification check, not a representation of every subsequent legal change.

entity_scope: Connecticut producers/refiners; dealer-operated service stations; specified exempt facilities
observation: Restrictions address producer/refiner station operation through employees, subsidiaries, commissioned agents and fee contractors. Temporary operation is regulated; specified state functions and a narrowly dated single training/test/advertising station exception are retained. OLR distinguishes ordinary wholesale jobbers from producers/refiners.
limits: Not a prohibition on all wholesale supply or property ownership. OLR is explanatory, not a court ruling applying the law to Getty or Consumers. Tax-distributor status is a different legal permission.

pages_or_locator: AN 2002(1): Diesel Fuel Distributors; Motor Vehicle Fuels Distributors; Gasohol Distributors; issued February 25, 2002
observation: GETTY PETROLEUM MARKETING INC appears separately in all three categories: Diesel Fuel Distributors (tax type 50); Motor Vehicle Fuels Distributors (tax type 52); Gasohol Distributors (tax type 57). The list describes licensed status as of January 1, 2002.
limits: One entity snapshot across three categories, not three businesses or transactions. Licensed tax-distribution channel only, not actual sales, import origin, station-operation permission, land ownership, affiliation with the other Getty entry or current status. Shared listed address does not establish ownership.
